transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus function using an explicit `slice: &mut [T]` receiver parameter, named public target, and the generated `final(slice)@ == slice_reversed(old(slice)@)` ensures clause.

Preserved the target flow `half_len = self.len() / 2`, `Range { start, end } = self.as_mut_ptr_range()`, raw front/back half construction with `from_raw_parts_mut(start, half_len)` and `from_raw_parts_mut(end.sub(half_len), half_len)`, and the final `revswap(front_half, back_half, half_len)` call.
Reused the reviewed `core::slice::as_mut_ptr_range` pointer-range/final-frame shape locally instead of re-proving raw start/end pointer provenance.
Isolated the unsafe raw half construction operations `from_raw_parts_mut` and `end.sub(half_len)` as named boundaries with local length/start-pointer facts.

Kept the private `revswap` helper executable with length checks, the `split_at_mut(n)` reborrow point isolated as a no-mutation boundary, and the `while i < n` loop that performs the source `mem::swap(&mut a[i], &mut b[n - 1 - i])` operation through a per-iteration boundary.

Added named raw-half partition, revswap loop-result, and whole-slice final-frame bridges to connect the source raw-derived half-slice mutations back to the generated reverse postcondition without making the public target external.
